sentences.text: Shri R.Sonvane, learned counsel for petitioner.

Shri.Akash Sharma, learned counsel for respondent/
Heard.

By this revision petition u/S.397 of the Cr.P.C, petitioner has challenged the order of the I Addl.
Sessions Judge, Neemuch dated 10/5/2019 whereby the appeal filed by the petitioner has been dismissed and judgment of the Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Neemuch in Criminal Trial No.354/2010 dated 23/8/2018 convicting the petitioner for offence u/S.7(1) read with Sec.16(1)(a)(1) and Sec.7(3) & Rule 50(1) read with Sec.16(1)(a) (2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentencing him for six - six months RI along with the fine of Rs.1500-1500 and default sentence of 1-1 month.

A complaint was filed before the trial court by the Food Inspector with the plea that on 21/12/2009 at 5.00 PM Inspector Raju Solanki had done the inspection of the shop of the petitioner and had found that the petitioner had collected packets of oil, ghee, sugar, milk cream and pure ghee for sale,
but he was not having the valid licence for the period 2009-10.

He had informed about taking the sample for analysis and had followed the due procedure for the same and had sent it to Public Analyst and as per the report, the sample of ghee was adulterated and was misbranded.
Hence, the complaint was filed after sanction for prosecution and notice u/S.13(2) was given to the petitioner.
The trial court had framed the charge for the aforesaid offences and the petitioner had abjured the guilt, therefore, trial has taken place.

Before the trial court the oral as well as the documentary evidence was produced and trial court had found the petitioner guilty of the offences and convicted and sentenced him in the manner indicated above.
Appeal preferred by the petitioner u/S.374 of the Cr.P.C has been dismissed by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge.

Learned counsel for petitioner submits that u/S.16(a) of the Act only the Judicial Magistrate I Class specially empowered by the State government is competent to conduct the trial, but the same has not been done.

He further submits that the trial court has committed an error in trying the case as warrant case instead of summary case and that proper opportunity of hearing was not granted to the petitioner to cross examine the public analyst.
Learned counsel for respondent has supported the impugned judgment.

Having heard the learned counsel for parties and on perusal of the record, it is noticed that the Ashok Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152777534/
1 offences under the provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act as mentioned above have duly been proved.
PW.2 Raju Solanki, the Food Inspector has disclosed in detail the manner of collection of sample from the shop of the petitioner and storage of item such as sugar, milk cream, ghee etc. in the shop without a valid licence.

sentences.text: His statement also reveals that the seizure was made by following the due process and samples were sent to Public Analyst, Food Examination Laboratory, Bhopal vide Ex.P/12

entities.text: Public Analyst, Food Examination Laboratory, Bhopal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: the receipt of which was produced as Ex.P/13.
The report Ex.P/17 received along with the letter dated 2 /2/2010 has duly been proved wherein the sample was found to be adulterated and misbranded.

The statement of PW.2 Rajul Solanki is duly supported by PW.1 Vijay Singh Solanki,
PW.3 Vipin and PW.4 H.P. Mishra.
PW.4 is the Public Analyst who during the relevant time was posted at State Food Laboratory, Bhopal and who had analyzed the food sample.
He had disclosed in detail the factum of adulteration and misbranding and has proved the report Ex.P.17.

PW.4 has also disclosed that the samples were examined by DGHS process and in the sample of milk cream pure ghee, there was no date of packing and manufacturing number was NIL and no date of manufacturing and the sample was misbranded.
The BADAYON test was negative and the ghee was adulterated.
Both the courts below have after examining the evidence in detail has reached to the same conclusion.

So far as the submission of the counsel for petitioner that the Judicial Magistrate I Class who had conducted the trial was not specifically empowered by the State is concerned, the record reflects that no such objection was raised by the petitioner at the stage of trial.
Hence the prosecution had no opportunity to bring on record the necessary documents in respect of empowerment of Judicial Magistrate by the State government u/S.16-A of the Act.
At the appellate stage also no such argument was advanced.
Hence, it is not open to the petitioner to raise such an argument for the first time before this court.

So far as the objection of the petitioner that proper opportunity was not given to the petitioner to cross examine PW.4 H.P. Mishra, the record reflects that counsel for petitioner was given opportunity for two days to cross examine the witness but the same was not availed by the petitioner.
This argument has duly been considered by the court below and rejected it.

So far as the argument that the summary trial was converted into warrant trial without giving notice to the petitioner is concerned, the court below in para 20 of the judgment has duly considered this argument.
It has been rightly noted that no objection was raised by the petitioner when the procedure of warrant trial was adopted.
That apart, the counsel for petitioner has also failed to point out any prejudice which has been caused on account of adopting the process of warrant trial.

Counsel for petitioner has placed reliance upon the judgment of the supreme court in the matter of Khem Chand Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh 1994 Cr.LJ 253 but in that case the adulteration was of minor nature and the offence had taken place 20 years back.

He has also placed reliance upon the judgment of the Supreme Court in the matter of T. Barai Vs. Henry Ah Hoe and another 1983 Cr.LJ 164, but that was a case relating to the effect of West Bengal State Amendment Act, 1973.

The State of Bihar 1980 Cr.LJ 2419 which relates to the effect of inordinate delay in sending the sample without explanation wherein sample was found to be containing dead and living ants, hence it was rendered unfit for scientific analysis.

He has also placed reliance upon the single bench judgment of Andhra Pradesh High Court in the case of Ravinder Kumar Vs. State of A.P. 1997 All India Prevention of Food Adulteration Journal 239 wherein trying of warrant case as summons case has been found to be illegal, but in the present case summons case has been tried as warrant case which is permissible u/S.259 of the Cr.P.C

Having regard to the aforesaid, I am of the opinion that the impugned order passed by the court below in respect of conviction and sentence of the petitioner for the offences as mentioned above does not suffer from any error and no case for interference is made out.
The revision petition is accordingly dismissed.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Learned counsel for petitioner submits that u/S.16(a) of the Act only the Judicial Magistrate I Class specially empowered by the State government is competent to conduct the trial, but the same has not been done.

He has also placed reliance upon the single bench judgment of Andhra Pradesh High Court in the case of Ravinder Kumar Vs. State of A.P. 1997 All India Prevention of Food Adulteration Journal 239 wherein trying of warrant case as summons case has been found to be illegal, but in the present case summons case has been tried as warrant case which is permissible u/S.259 of the Cr.P.C
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
So far as the submission of the counsel for petitioner that the Judicial Magistrate I Class who had conducted the trial was not specifically empowered by the State is concerned, the record reflects that no such objection was raised by the petitioner at the stage of trial.
Hence the prosecution had no opportunity to bring on record the necessary documents in respect of empowerment of Judicial Magistrate by the State government u/S.16-A of the Act.

2 upon the judgment of single bench of Patna High Court in the case of Jagat Narayan Sah & another Vs. The State of Bihar 1980 Cr.LJ 2419 which relates to the effect of inordinate delay in sending the sample without explanation wherein sample was found to be containing dead and living ants, hence it was rendered unfit for scientific analysis.
In the present case, firstly no argument was advanced relating to delay and even otherwise there is no material on record to show that the sample had become unfit on account of the delay.
